site.title: THE REAL WINDY CITY LEDGER
site.kicker: Cheyenne, Wyoming — public documents in, verifiable evidence out.
site.tagline: Wind belongs on the prairie. Not in the minutes.
site.voice_note: Written in the tradition of Cheyenne's plainest public commenters: read the statute, quote the record, sign your name. Not produced by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any individual — named or otherwise — or any candidate, campaign, or political committee.

question_of_the_week.headline: Does the city clerk certify the referendum — and does a judge let it stand?
question_of_the_week.body: Organizers turned in roughly 3,200 signatures; 2,739 valid Cheyenne-registered 2024 voters are required under the Title 22 referendum statute. The city attorney is simultaneously asking a district court whether annexations must be fought under W.S. 15-1-409 instead. Until both questions resolve, Ordinance No. 4687 — the largest annexation in city history — sits in suspension's doorway.
question_of_the_week.watch_for: Clerk's final count; declaratory-judgment filing; any motion invoking W.S. 22-23-1005/1007.

timeline.label: Administrative warrant ordinance advances 7-3. A resident tells the council a municipal judge can't issue the city's own search warrants.
County commissioners unanimously approve Project Jade — 1.8 GW now, potentially 10 GW, the largest AI campus proposal in the country.
Warrant ordinance passes 7-3, but 'discover' and 'determine' are struck. 'Verify' survives. Public comment moved the text.
BOPU routine sampling finds Cupriavidus gilardii in the reclaimed water system. Public won't be told for ~4 months.
BOPU revokes Goat Systems LLC's discharge privileges — the contractor on Meta's $800M data center.
Iron Guard's 800-unit, up-to-5,600-worker 'man camp' plan surfaces — bigger than 84 Wyoming towns.
12-month data-center moratorium fails 8-1 after four hours of testimony. Moody is the only yes.
Iron Guard withdraws the man camp after weeks of backlash; county keeps the contact list in case it returns.
Council advances Microsoft's 3,500-acre annexation. 'You are granting municipal jurisdiction to a 3,500-acre ghost project,' a resident testifies. 'Premeditated regulatory arbitrage.'
BOPU confirms the rare bacterium was traced to Meta's contractor; city bans all data-center fill-and-flush discharges. Rep. Hageman writes Mark Zuckerberg.
Ordinance No. 4687 passes 6-3 just before 2 a.m. — the largest annexation in Cheyenne's history. Rep. Ann Lucas warns it is 'likely irreversible.'
Volunteers file the referendum petition: about 3,200 signatures against a 2,739-signature requirement.
After an unagendized post-executive-session vote, the council directs the city attorney to ask a court whether the referendum process even applies. Moody dissents.
Secretary of State Chuck Gray tells the council: don't 'abuse legal processes and procedures to bog down Cheyenne residents' constitutional rights under the initiative process.'
Primary sets November: Kallas v. Brand (Ward 1, open), Rose v. Storey-Huylar (Ward 2, open), Esquibel v. Bryant (Ward 3).

Same week, Finance Committee hears the $186,500 roundabout re-study. 'You are quite literally paying a premium consultant to study a study of your own failed design.' It passes the full council Aug. 25 anyway.
County commissioners approve Vantage's 'Project Latigo' zone change — 1,835 acres, its own gas plant, no public commenters at the planning stage.
General election. Three council seats — and, if the clerk certifies and the court allows, the annexation referendum.
